# Storage access denied
A copy activity returning 403 Forbidden usually needs an identity and network review. Capture the activity name, correlation ID, and UTC timestamp. Verify the managed identity has Storage Blob Data Contributor on the intended container, rather than assuming subscription Reader is sufficient. Check storage firewall rules and the private endpoint DNS route. Test with a narrow read before retrying a write. Escalate permission changes through the approved owner. Do not paste credentials into incident notes.

# Integration runtime timeout
A pipeline timeout may follow source latency or insufficient runtime capacity. Review integration runtime CPU and active concurrent jobs. Compare source query duration with normal baselines. Reduce batch size or concurrency as a controlled experiment before scaling resources. Use bounded retries with exponential backoff for transient failures. A retry does not correct a schema mismatch. Record the timing, test, and result in the incident timeline.

# Schema contract mismatch
A renamed source column can break downstream mappings. Compare incoming headers and data types with the versioned contract. Confirm whether a missing field is optional before supplying defaults. Review source release notes and the destination mapping. Quarantine incompatible records rather than silently dropping them. Validate the corrected mapping on a synthetic sample and reconcile row counts before resuming the scheduled ingestion.

# Missing records and watermark gaps
When source and target row counts differ, reconcile unique business keys, not only totals. Inspect ingestion watermark predicates, time zones, and late-arriving data. Check rejected-record logs and the expected partition range. Separate missing keys from changed values. Never rerun a non-idempotent load without a rollback plan. Capture the exact affected window and agree the reprocessing boundary with the data owner.

# Duplicate loads and idempotency
Duplicate business keys may indicate overlapping batch windows or retries after partial commits. Inspect the batch identifier and checkpoint state. Confirm merge keys and deduplication ordering. An idempotent rerun produces the same logical result without adding duplicate rows. Use a staging table and controlled merge when appropriate. Reconcile keys and aggregates after remediation, then document the run and rollback evidence.

# Privacy review before sharing
Before exporting a dataset, identify direct identifiers such as names, emails, and phone numbers. Review quasi-identifiers that may identify a person in combination. Mask or remove fields according to the approved purpose. Tokens are pseudonyms and should not be assumed anonymous. Generalization trades detail for lower granularity. Inspect residual signals, small groups, and free-text fields manually before sharing an approved extract.
